about.title: Personal Injury Help in Fairfield, California
about.longDescription: Fairfield sits where I-80 carries the daily push between the Bay Area and Sacramento, and its local streets absorb a share of that load. In 2025, the most recent final crash year, public records show 645 injury collisions inside the city, with 912 people injured and 7 lives lost. The corridors with the highest collision counts were I-80, Air Base Parkway, North Texas Street, and Travis Boulevard, and reports tend to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., as the work week winds down. Behind each of those numbers is a person dealing with doctor visits, a car in the shop, missed shifts, and an adjuster who keeps calling. That is where LawProactive comes in. We are a free service, not a law firm. We do not give legal advice and we do not represent you. What we do is connect Fairfield residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases like yours across Solano County. That attorney reviews your situation at no charge, and if you decide to move forward, they work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives most injury claims a two-year window, and less time when a public agency is involved, so reaching out early keeps your options open.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Fairfield Claim

items.title: Two years for most claims, less against the government
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a city, county, or state agency may be responsible, a claim often has to be filed within six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you share some responsibility for a crash on Travis Boulevard, your recovery is reduced by your percentage, but you are not barred from recovering.

items.title: No cap on pain-and-suffering damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California does not limit non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. An attorney can explain how these losses are documented.

items.title: Contingency fees, so no bill up front
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency. They are paid only if there is a recovery, which means you can get a case review without worrying about hourly charges.

items.question: Where do collisions cluster in Fairfield according to public records?
items.answer: For the 2025 final crash year, public records list I-80, Air Base Parkway, North Texas Street, and Travis Boulevard as the corridors with the highest collision counts in Fairfield. Citywide there were 645 injury collisions, 912 people injured, and 7 deaths. These are neutral counts that reflect traffic volume, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Fairfield?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date of injury. If a government entity such as the city or Caltrans may be responsible, you often have only six months to file a formal claim first. An attorney can confirm which deadline applies to you.

items.question: What if the crash was partly my fault?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault. Your compensation is reduced by your share of responsibility, but you can still recover for the portion that was not your fault. Insurers sometimes overstate your share, which is one reason to have an attorney review the facts.
